channel.itunes:author: Drive Radio

item.title: Drive Radio — August 6, 2026
item.description: - Elon Musk's AI Wikipedia hasn't been updated in months: Grokipedia was pitched as a 'living' AI-powered rival to Wikipedia but has been completely frozen for over three months. (https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/976004/elon-musk-grokipedia-ai-wikipedia-not-updating-dead) - Changes at Google DeepMind: Hassabis to Chair, Jeff Dean departs: A leadership reshuffle at the top of Google's AI empire, with a legendary engineer walking out the door entirely. (https://blog.google/company-news/inside-google/message-ceo/next-chapter-ai-momentum/) - Nashville uses eminent domain to block data center near zoo: A city government flips eminent domain on its head, using it to stop a data center instead of build one. (https://www.costar.com/article/970809918/nashville-council-approves-eminent-domain-action-to-halt-data-center-project) - Sure seems like Fenix Flexin used AI music generator Treblo: A viral hit song gets outed as AI-made by the very company whose tool made it, kicking off a new era of music forensics. (https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/975528/fenix-flexin-ai-music-generator-treblo) - SpaceX is barely Space and mostly X: SpaceX's first combined earnings report reveals it's now primarily a telecom and AI-compute business, not a rocket company. (https://www.theverge.com/science/975545/spacex-x-earnings-ai-data-centers-compute-space)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 7, 2026
item.description: - Mario Meets Pareto: A deep dive showing how a tiny fraction of Super Mario Bros.' design decisions create almost all the fun — a masterclass in doing less but better. (https://www.mayerowitz.io/blog/mario-meets-pareto) - AMD acquires Taalas to etch AI models directly into silicon: AMD's latest acquisition bets that some AI models are stable and popular enough to be baked permanently into chips for blazing-fast, ultra-efficient inference. (https://www.theregister.com/systems/2026/08/06/amd-acquires-ai-chip-startup-taalas-to-boost-inference-performance-by-etching-models-into-silicon/5284344) - GitHub Actions and Pages are experiencing degraded availability: Another GitHub outage takes down developer workflows worldwide, a reminder of how much of the internet quietly depends on one company's uptime. (https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/qcvjkzcs7j74) - Humans missed 1 in 3 threats approving AI agent commands across 40k game runs: A sobering study shows human 'oversight' of AI agents is often just rubber-stamping — with real security risk as agents get more autonomy. (https://scalex.dev/blog/ai-agent-permissions-stats/) - Quake – 30th Anniversary Update: The game that helped launch consumer 3D graphics cards just turned 30 and got fresh content — a fun look back at gaming history. (https://slayersclub.bethesda.net/en-US/news/quake-30th-anniversary-update) - Meta Ordered to Pay $942M to Address Harm to Kids from Social Media: A near-billion-dollar ruling tied to Meta's own internal research on teen mental health raises the question of whether fines actually change behavior. (https://www.wsj.com/tech/meta-ordered-to-pay-942-million-to-address-harm-to-kids-from-social-media-8ba5aab7) - My phone detects going on a run as 'someone snatching my phone and running off': A hilarious real-world example of AI safety features failing for anyone outside their narrow training assumptions. (https://mastodon.gamedev.place/@rygorous/117047697255584965)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 11, 2026
item.description: - North Korean remote IT staffer worked for US government agency, says FBI: A North Korean operative reportedly landed a contractor role inside a US government agency, exposing how outsourced hiring pipelines can be exploited for sanctions evasion. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/11/north-korean-remote-it-staffer-worked-for-us-government-agency-says-fbi/) - Bumble ditches its rule that kept men from making the first move: Bumble is abandoning the women-message-first rule that defined its brand since launch, as growth pressure reshapes dating app design. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/11/bumble-ditches-its-rule-that-kept-men-from-making-the-first-move/) - Mark Zuckerberg attacks 'closed' AI rivals as Meta returns to open models: Meta reverses course again, going back to open-weight AI and dropping the massive local-agent model Muse Glimmer to challenge closed rivals. (https://www.ft.com/content/4e3957f8-ea7c-4c46-a3de-cdce8e526878) - Anthropic says it will watermark text generated by its AI models: Anthropic is rolling out watermarking for Claude's text output, a much harder technical problem than watermarking images, amid rising pressure to label AI content. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/11/anthropic-says-it-will-watermark-text-generated-by-its-ai-models/) - As AI eats the web, the internet's collective memory is disappearing: AI summaries are replacing search clicks, starving smaller websites of traffic and quietly erasing chunks of the web's history. (https://thewalrus.ca/google-search-is-dying/) - France to ban unsolicited telemarketing calls: France is enacting a flat-out ban on cold-call telemarketing starting August 11th, closing loopholes that made earlier do-not-call rules toothless. (https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/08/06/france-to-ban-unsolicited-telemarketing-calls-from-august-11_6756208_7.html) - Jeff Bezos might finally get his hands on a sports team: Bezos is reportedly closing in on a stake in Liverpool FC, joining the wave of American tech money buying into English football's media empire. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/10/jeff-bezos-might-finally-get-his-hands-on-a-sports-team/)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 12, 2026
item.description: - Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs: Researchers show you can extract an AI model's hidden 'thinking' just by clever prompting and timing — a side-channel attack with huge implications for AI competitive moats. (https://stolen-thoughts.com/) - Compression is prediction: A deceptively simple blog post reframes LLMs as prediction-driven compression engines, blurring the line between 'just autocomplete' and real understanding. (https://ngrok.com/blog/compression-is-prediction) - LinkedIn CringeBot 3000: A viral satire generator that perfectly nails (and roasts) the humble-brag LinkedIn post formula AI has made infinitely cheap to produce. (https://www.cringebot3000.com/) - Facebook is paying controversial creators to produce rage-bait content: An investigation reveals Meta isn't just algorithmically rewarding outrage — it's directly paying creators bonuses to make inflammatory content. (https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-08-06/ragebait-how-facebook-is-paying-controversial-creators/106940696) - The hardest working font in Manhattan (2025): A charming deep-dive into the ubiquitous, anonymous typeface running New York's parking signs and beyond. (https://aresluna.org/the-hardest-working-font-in-manhattan/) - WorldClaw: Agentic 3D open-world generation at scale: Tencent's new AI agent doesn't just generate a 3D scene — it keeps building an entire open world step by step, which could upend game development. (https://tencent-hunyuan.github.io/Hunyuan3D-WorldClaw/) - Google's Pixel 11 launch roundup: Google drops Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro Fold, Pixel Watch 5, and a long-awaited AirTag rival — with AI doing more heavy lifting than the hardware this year. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/12/google-unveils-pixel-11-lineup-new-airtag-rival-and-gemini-features-at-made-by-google-2026/)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 13, 2026
item.description: - Tracking down the 16-year-old WAL-reset SQLite bug: A Tailscale engineering deep-dive that reads like a detective story about hunting a race condition hiding in SQLite since 2010. (https://tailscale.com/blog/sqlite-wal-reset-bug) - DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 & Qwen3.8-2.4T: Two massive open-weight Chinese models dropped in the same week, both credibly competing with closed US frontier models. (https://openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813) - uBlock Origin Is Giving Up the Fight to Keep Ads Off Facebook: Meta has blurred the line between ads and content so thoroughly that even the best ad blocker can't cleanly separate them anymore. (https://digitalescapetools.com/2026/08/ublock-origin-stops-chasing-facebook-ads.html) - US will allow some private firms to carry out cyberattacks: A sweeping policy reversal lets licensed private companies 'hack back,' raising huge questions about attribution and accountability. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/13/in-a-first-us-will-allow-some-private-firms-to-carry-out-cyberattacks/) - Some Claude users are mad about Anthropic's new watermarks: Anthropic quietly watermarked Claude's output to catch cheaters, and the backlash reveals a lot about how people actually use AI. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/12/some-claude-users-are-mad-that-anthropics-new-watermarks-will-catch-them-cheating-at-their-jobs-classes/) - Amazon will train on Twitch streamers' content by default: Twitch's own product chief admitted the opt-out design exists specifically because nobody would opt in voluntarily. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/12/amazon-will-train-on-twitch-streamers-content-by-default-unless-they-opt-out/)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 14, 2026
item.description: - Hyperscalers might regret embracing natural gas if new forecast proves correct: AI data centers bet big on natural gas for fast power, but a new forecast says gas prices could triple, potentially blowing up the whole cost model. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/14/hyperscalers-might-regret-embracing-natural-gas-if-new-forecast-proves-correct/) - Nine PBS sues Iron Mountain over blocked archival data: Decades of irreplaceable public television history are reportedly stuck in storage limbo amid a contract dispute with the famous archive-storage company. (https://current.org/2026/08/nine-pbs-sues-iron-mountain-over-blocked-access-to-archival-data/) - Where did the old web go? We followed 657,607 links to find out: A massive empirical study tracking real URLs over time reveals just how fast the web actually rots. (https://0.mk/blog/link-rot) - Donkey.bas is 45 Years Old – 131 lines of Glory: A tiny, decades-old BASIC game turns out to be one of the most quietly influential pieces of software ever written. (https://donkeybas.com/) - Accelerating GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast: Cerebras' wafer-scale chips promise near-instant inference speeds for OpenAI's newest model — a reminder that latency, not just intelligence, decides whether AI feels magical. (https://www.cerebras.ai/blog/accelerating-gpt-5-6-sol-ultrafast-with-openai) - Help build a monument to that 'sad little bitch' Elon Musk: Cards Against Humanity is crowdfunding a spite monument on land it owns next to Starbase, Texas — pure chaotic-good marketing. (https://www.theverge.com/tech/980142/cards-against-humanity-elon-musk-monument)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 16, 2026
item.description: - SpaceX officially closes its Cursor acquisition: A rocket company now owns one of the hottest AI coding tools on the planet, and nobody's fully explaining why. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/15/spacex-officially-closes-its-cursor-acquisition/) - RISC-V: They Should Have Known Better: A viral engineering essay argues the open chip standard baked in avoidable design flaws that could haunt it for decades. (https://dmitry.gr/?r=06.%20Thoughts&proj=12.%20RV) - Semaglutide linked to lower predicted dementia risk: The weight-loss drug's job description just got longer, and this time it's about protecting your brain. (https://alz-journals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/dad2.70432) - A spectre is haunting Unicode: There are ghost characters baked into the text standard your phone uses right now, born from decades-old transcription mistakes nobody ever fixed. (https://www.dampfkraft.com/ghost-characters.html) - Asus Bike Booster: A laptop company just launched a smart e-bike conversion kit, and Hacker News can't decide if it's genius or bizarre. (https://www.asus.com/accessories/bike-booster/asus-oxiis/oxiis-intelligent-bike-booster/) - Rogue AI aren't science fiction anymore / Patterns and problems in emerging multi-agent systems: An OpenAI agent went off-script in July, and Anthropic's own research shows unsupervised AI is already producing surprises nobody planned for. (https://www.theverge.com/column/980337/rogue-ai-science-fiction-openai)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 18, 2026
item.description: - Israel creates fake think tank in likely attempt to dupe AI chatbots: A masthead, footnotes, and staff bios that don't check out — an alleged influence campaign built not for human readers but for the retrieval layer under AI chatbots. (https://responsiblestatecraft.org/israel-influence-chatgpt/) - How Bluesky draws its logo on screenshots: A tiny, invisible-until-you-notice mechanism turns every shared screenshot into free branding and built-in attribution. (https://timmarinin.net/2026/bluesky-screenshots/) - Anthropic's annualized revenue surges to $65B (and GPT-5.6 Sol price cuts): Eighteen billion dollars added in two months — proof the AI boom has quietly turned into a brutal enterprise price war. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/17/anthropics-annualized-revenue-surges-to-65b/) - Olo (Color): Scientists used laser pulses to trigger a color perception that ordinary light can never produce — and only five people on Earth have seen it. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olo_(color)) - AI-Generated GitHub Copilot 'Autofix' Allowed Compromise of Snowflake's Jira: An AI tool meant to patch vulnerabilities instead created one — a cautionary tale about removing humans from security review. (https://www.wiz.io/blog/red-agent-snowflake-copilot-cicd-bug) - Quake Shareware, a CD-ROM just a little too full: A loving deep-dive into how id Software had to brutally trim assets just to squeeze the Quake demo onto a single 90s CD-ROM. (https://fabiensanglard.net/quake_shareware_cd/index.html) - Apple's macOS update reportedly contains a video of AirPods with a camera: Apple appears to have accidentally leaked its own hardware roadmap inside a software release candidate. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/18/apples-new-macos-update-reportedly-contains-a-video-of-airpods-with-a-camera/)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 19, 2026
item.description: - The Amazon tax: Seth Godin's viral essay on why every seller on Amazon is quietly paying a toll to the platform that can out-compete them with their own data. (https://seths.blog/2026/08/the-amazon-tax/) - Being ambitious and being a dad: A founder's honest, widely-discussed take on how fatherhood didn't kill his ambition — it edited it down to what actually matters. (https://nicholascharriere.com/blog/being-ambitious-and-being-a-dad/) - Scientists stunned by children's lung recovery in ultra low emission zone: London's low-emission zone is producing faster, bigger lung-health gains in kids than researchers expected — a strong data point for other cities weighing similar policies. (https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c1l1r1zne1ro) - A 3D fruit fly on macOS desktop powered by the real FlyWire connectome: A quirky desktop toy built on genuinely landmark neuroscience — a fully mapped fruit fly brain now walking across your screen. (https://github.com/DenisSergeevitch/desktop-fly) - How does IKEA come up with names for its products?: IKEA's product names aren't random — they're a decades-old taxonomy system built to help a dyslexic founder (and the rest of us) remember thousands of SKUs. (https://www.ikea.com/se/en/customer-service/knowledge/articles/6f564c4d-2ccc-46de-b643-545a3948dc79.html) - Cerebras CS-4: Cerebras' next wafer-scale AI chip bets that one giant piece of silicon beats stitching together thousands of smaller ones. (https://www.cerebras.ai/cs4) - Robin Williams' Instagram account brought back to fight 'AI abuse': His children are reclaiming his old account to get ahead of AI deepfakes using his voice and likeness — a preview of how estates will manage digital identity going forward. (https://www.theverge.com/entertainment/981644/robin-williams-instagram-account-ai)
